findings.title: Non-tcpCloser backend never gets EOF, so the proxy can hang forever
findings.explanation: The function now waits for both copy goroutines before returning and closing the conns. If the type assertion fails (e.g. a custom ns.forwardDialFunc returns a wrapped net.Conn without CloseRead/CloseWrite), nothing tells the backend the client has finished sending when client->backend reaches EOF. A backend that waits for EOF before replying or closing never finishes, so io.Copy(client, backend) blocks forever. The goroutines, backend fd, client endpoint and the RegisterIPPortIdentity mapping then leak. The old code avoided this by tearing down both conns after the first direction ended. The comment calls the assertion 'should always succeed', but nothing enforces it.
findings.suggestion: When !backendIsTCPCloser, fall back to the old behaviour. For example, call backend.Close() in the client->backend goroutine after the copy finishes, or return after the first connClosed value. Alternatively, log or handle the failed assertion explicitly instead of silently skipping the half-close.

findings.title: Half-closed connection can stay open indefinitely with no idle timeout
findings.explanation: Before this change, the first direction to finish (EOF or error) closed both connections. Now, after one side sends FIN, forwardTCP keeps the goroutines, sockets and the IP-port identity mapping alive until the other side also closes. A peer that never closes its half (an idle client after the backend has closed, or a backend that ignores FIN) holds these resources until keepalive, if any, detects a dead peer. An alive but idle peer is never detected. The HUp watcher only cancels the dial context, so it does not help here.
findings.suggestion: After the first connClosed value arrives, set a read/write deadline (or a timer that closes both conns) for the remaining direction, so a half-closed connection can't hang forever.
